Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 28 s. 2023 APR 19 2023 HON. MARIETTA T. SUMAYLO Vice Mayor Dauis, Bohol Dear Vice Mayor Sumaylo: This has reference to your letter dated December 14, 2022 seeking intervention from the Department for the immediate release of the salaries of the Job Order/Contract of Service being withheld. Per your representation, the following are the antecedent facts of the case: The salaries of Job Orders (JOS) of the Office of the Vice Mayor and Office of the Sangguniang Bayan of the Municipality of Dauis from November 2022 up to present are being withheld. Said salaries are to be taken from the appropriations under the said offices. Memorandum No. 39, s.2022 dated November 14, 2022 was issued by Mayor Roman Bullen, advising the Municipal Budget Officer, Municipal Accountant, Municipal Treasurer and Human Resource Management Office to refrain from acting on any voucher/payroll with regard to any claim for wages/salaries of the JOS from the said Offices. Such Memorandum was issued based on the Legal Opinion dated November 15, 2022 rendered by Atty. Handel L. Lagunay, Provincial Legal Officer of Bohol, in response to the query on the legality of the Vice Mayor and the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan to hire JOS. The said opinion reiterated this Department's Legal Opinion No. 34, s. 2014, dated October 27, 2014. Vice Mayor Sumaylo also wrote to the Provincial Legal Office, requesting for reconsideration/reevaluation to the earlier legal opinion. However, the Provincial Legal Office stood that there is no cogent reason to disturb the said opinion. Meanwhile, Vice Mayor contended that the JO are still entitled to collect their salaries and wages for work actually rendered as de facto personnel of LGU- Dauis Bohol. Further, not paying the salaries of the JOS for work actually rendered would constitute unjust enrichment in favor of the Municipal LGU to the prejudice of the said personnel. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54 CamScanner

Hence, the herein request. At the outset, the Department stands with Legal Opinion No. 34, s.2014, the penultimate paragraph of which states: As a general rule, all contracts of services and job orders shall be entered into by the local chief executive of the local government unit, except in cases where there is an ordinance passed by the sanggunian specifically authorizing the vice-mayor or vice-governor to enter into contracts on behalf of the local government unit. Hence, regardless of the source of fund, it is only the local chief executive that has the authority to hire JOs/COS, unless there is an ordinance specifically authorizing the vice mayor or vice governor to hire them. In view thereof, all legal opinion rendered by the Department inconsistent herewith are superseded accordingly. As to the contract executed between the JO and the employer, we believe that the same is an unenforceable contract — which is governed by the following provisions of the Civil Code of the Philippines, viz: ARTICLE 1403. The following contracts are unenforceable, unless they are ratified: (I) Those entered into in the name of another person by one who has been given no authority or legal representation, or who has acted beyond his powers; xxx ARTICLE 1404. Unauthorized contracts are governed by article 1317 and the principles of agency in Title X of this Book. Meanwhile, Article 1317 of the Civil Code states: ARTICLE 1317. No one may contract in the name of another without being authorized by the latter, or unless he has by law a right to represent him. A contract entered into in the name of another by one who has no authority or legal representation, or who has acted beyond his powers, shall be unenforceable, unless it is ratified, expressly or impliedly, by the person on whose behalf it has been executed, before it is revoked by the other contracting party. Accordingly, we recommend for the sanggunian to enact an ordinance, relative to the hiring of JOS, for the contract to be ratified. Ratification may be effected expressly or tacitly. It is understood that there is a tacit ratification if, with knowledge of the reason which renders the contract voidable and such reason having ceased, the person who has a right to invoke it should execute an act which necessarily implies an intention to waive his rightl. Ratification cleanses the contract from all its defect from the moment 1 Article 1393, Civil Code of the Philippines Page 2 of 3 CamScanner

it was constituted2. Be that as it may, this opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BYA HORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AT AN VI R.
